items.title: [Bug]: schema-invalid jobs index prevents fallback to a healthy jobs.json
items.description:
### Bug Type
Portal: website not loading or showing stale data

### Description
The browser's fallback from `jobs-index.json` to `jobs.json` handles HTTP / JSON-decoding failures, but not a successful JSON response with an invalid jobs schema. If the index answers HTTP 200 with `{ "nope": 1 }` while `jobs.json` contains valid postings, `loadJobs` returns an error and zero jobs without requesting the healthy full dataset.

Verified against `main` at `c73256709`; the relevant files are unchanged from that commit. This is a deterministic fault-injection reproduction, not evidence that production currently serves an invalid index.

### Steps to Reproduce
Run from the repository root:

```sh
node --input-type=module <<'JS'
import { loadJobs } from './site/src/data/jobs-source.js';
const calls = [];
const fetchImpl = async (url) => {
  calls.push(url);
  return {
    ok: true,
    json: async () => url.endsWith('jobs-index.json')
      ? { nope: 1 }
      : { jobs: [{ job_id: 'job_valid', title: 'Junior Engineer', company: 'Example' }] },
  };
};
const result = await loadJobs(fetchImpl, false);
console.log({ calls, jobs: result.jobs.length, error: result.error });
JS
```

Actual:

```text
calls: ['./jobs-index.json']
jobs: 0
error: 'jobs payload has no "jobs" array'
```

Expected: `jobs.json` is requested, its valid posting is returned, and `error` is null.

### Cause
In [`jobs-source.js`](https://github.com/ambicuity/New-Grad-Jobs/blob/c73256709/site/src/data/jobs-source.js), the inner `try/catch` protects only the index fetch/decode. `normalizeJobsPayload(payload)` runs after that catch, so a schema error goes straight to the outer failure handler and bypasses the fallback.

The existing “reports a malformed payload” test supplies only an invalid index. It does not provide a healthy full file or assert that fallback was attempted.

### Expected Behavior / Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Index loading is considered successful only after schema validation and normalization succeed.
- [ ] A schema-invalid index triggers a request for `jobs.json`.
- [ ] A valid full payload restores jobs and returns `error: null`.
- [ ] A valid empty index (`jobs: []`) remains a successful empty result, without fallback.
- [ ] When both candidates fail, the loader resolves with an explicit error rather than rejecting or silently reporting success.
- [ ] Add deterministic tests for invalid index + healthy full payload, both invalid, and valid empty index; cover schema-invalid Brotli index payloads as applicable.

### Validation
Reproduced with the injected fetch above. Existing checks also pass: `vitest run src/lib/share.test.js src/data/data-sources.test.js test/seo.test.js` (**50 passed**).

Searched open and closed issues for index/fallback/malformed-payload reports; no issue tracking this specific jobs-loader recovery gap was found.

items.title: [Bug]: near-miss job share links point to static pages that are never generated
items.description:
### Bug Type
Portal: broken link or incorrect data displayed

### Description
“Copy link to this job” produces a static `/job/<job_id>/` URL for a near-miss posting, even though the SEO build generates these pages only for the curated dataset. The copied link therefore points to a page the deployment does not contain.

Verified against `main` at `c73256709`. The relevant source and fixture files are unchanged from that commit. This is reproduced locally using committed fixtures; no live posting counts are asserted.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Build the fixture site (`cd site && npm run build:fixtures`).
2. Open the board and enable **WIDEN SCOPE → internships & co-ops**.
3. Select the fixture posting `job_e001ffffffffffffffff` (Palantir, Software Engineer Intern - Summer 2027).
4. Click “Copy link to this job”. The URL is `https://jobs.riteshrana.engineer/job/job_e001ffffffffffffffff/` (or the equivalent preview origin).
5. Inspect `site/dist/job/job_e001ffffffffffffffff/index.html`: it does not exist. Opening the copied URL cannot restore that posting.

Independent local verification called `generateSeo` directly on `site/test/fixtures`: it generated 19 curated job pages, while the page for this near-miss ID was absent. Calling `jobShareUrl(mapJob(nearMiss), location)` returned the missing static-page URL.

### Cause
- [`share.js`](https://github.com/ambicuity/New-Grad-Jobs/blob/c73256709/site/src/lib/share.js) selects the static path for every valid `jobId`, without considering `nearMiss`.
- [`DashboardView.jsx`](https://github.com/ambicuity/New-Grad-Jobs/blob/c73256709/site/src/components/hiring/DashboardView.jsx) uses that helper for both curated and widened-scope rows.
- [`generate.mjs`](https://github.com/ambicuity/New-Grad-Jobs/blob/c73256709/site/scripts/seo/generate.mjs) reads `jobs.json` / `jobs-index.json`, not `jobs-extended.json`.

### Expected Behavior / Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Copied links for near misses open the board with the selected posting restored.
- [ ] The link includes every required `include` reason so the receiving browser loads the extended dataset and can display the posting, including postings with multiple reasons.
- [ ] Curated postings retain their existing static job-page links.
- [ ] Links work at the domain root and under a GitHub Pages subpath.
- [ ] Curated counts, feeds, and SEO job-page scope remain unchanged.
- [ ] Add deterministic unit coverage plus an integration/E2E case that opens a copied near-miss link in a fresh view.

### Validation and Related Issues
`vitest run src/lib/share.test.js src/data/data-sources.test.js test/seo.test.js`: **50 passed**. The gap is not exercised by those tests.

Related to #181, but distinct: the current React detail view and URL state already exist. This report concerns the wrong destination produced by the current share action specifically for the near-miss tier.

items.title: Privacy policy: Cloudflare proxies the site but is not disclosed
items.description:
Every request to jobs.riteshrana.engineer goes through Cloudflare before GitHub Pages: the responses carry `server: cloudflare`, `cf-ray` and `cf-cache-status`, and DNS resolves to Cloudflare addresses. Cloudflare also adds:

- `Report-To` / `NEL` headers, which ask browsers to report failed connections to `a.nel.cloudflare.com`;
- its Web Analytics beacon (`static.cloudflareinsights.com`), which every page's CSP blocks. It shows up as a console error and never runs.

No cookies are set. The privacy policy names only GitHub Pages as the host, so it needs a Cloudflare section, and the sharing, transfers, retention and security sections and the terms need updating to match.

Separately, the owner should disable Web Analytics automatic setup in the Cloudflare dashboard. That's a dashboard setting, not a code change.

items.title: [Bug]: Workday tenants that null locationsText publish out-of-region jobs and lose JobPosting JSON-LD
items.description:
### Bug Type

Scraper: incorrect job information (title, location, date)

### Description

The Workday adapter drops the location for tenants whose search payload returns `locationsText: null`, so those postings publish with an **empty location**. Two concrete consequences:

**1. The target-country gate is bypassed, and out-of-region jobs reach the curated board.**

`scripts/ngj/locations.py` deliberately treats an empty location as *unknown, not foreign* (module docstring, lines 18–21). That is correct for sources that genuinely omit locations — but these tenants do not omit it, the adapter simply never reads it. The location is still present, encoded in `externalPath` as the `/job/<Location>/` segment.

Result on the current published run: **90 curated jobs sit in Warsaw, Manila, Paris, Singapore, Prague, Lisbon, Stockholm, Riga, Blagnac, Torino, Kronberg, Bratislava and more** — 53 distinct non-target locations — on a board that advertises itself as US/Canada/India only. The filter that should have caught them ran against `""` and passed.

**2. 391 jobs lose their JobPosting structured data.**

`site/scripts/seo/jobposting.mjs:122` refuses to emit markup it cannot fill honestly:

```js
const location = locationProps(job.location);
if (!location) return { posting: null, reason: 'unresolvable location' };
```

Those pages still build and still appear in the sitemap, but carry no `JobPosting` JSON-LD, so they are effectively invisible to Google Jobs. **363 of 2877 curated jobs (12.6%) display an em-dash** for location (`site/src/lib/jobs.js:117`, `loc: raw.location || '—'`) and cannot be filtered by location.

All 363 affected jobs are Accenture. The other 1056 Workday jobs parse correctly, so the bug is tenant-shape-specific.

**Affected code** — `scripts/ngj/sources/workday.py:189`:

```python
'location': item.get('locationsText') or '',
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Fetch Accenture from its Workday tenant (`https://accenture.wd103.myworkdayjobs.com/AccentureCareers`). Confirmed live — the payload returns **both** location fields null while the URL still carries the city:

   ```json
   {
     "title": "Software Engineering New Associate (Fresh Diploma Graduate Program)",
     "locationsText": null,
     "postedLocations": null,
     "externalPath": "/job/Singapore/Software-Engineering-New-Associate--Fresh-Diploma-Graduate-Program-_R00144534"
   }
   ```

2. Run a scrape with `NGJ_OUTPUT_DIR=/tmp/ngj make run`.
3. Inspect `site/public/jobs.json`: 363 Workday jobs have `location: ""`.
4. Parse the `/job/<segment>/` out of each job's `url` — 53 distinct segments fail `is_valid_location()`; 90 jobs are out of region.
5. Run `npm run build` — the SEO plugin reports `2486 with JobPosting JSON-LD; skipped — unresolvable location: 391`.
6. Open any affected job page: no `JobPosting` JSON-LD in the source, and the board shows `—` where the location should be.

### Suggested Fix

Read the `/job/<Location>/` segment from `externalPath` as a fallback in `_to_job` (`scripts/ngj/sources/workday.py`):

```python
def _location_from_path(item: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    if item.get('locationsText'):
        return item['locationsText']
    match = re.match(r'^/job/([^/]+)/', item.get('externalPath') or '')
    return match.group(1).replace('-', ' ') if match else ''
```

This makes the 90 out-of-region jobs correctly fail the location gate, restores JSON-LD for the rest, and removes the em-dashes.

### Additional Context

**Regression tests worth adding** (both would have caught this the day the tenant's payload shape changed, and guard the next tenant that does the same):

- A Workday item with `locationsText: null` still yields a location derived from `externalPath`.
- A posting whose location resolves to a non-target country never reaches `jobs.json`.

**Verification performed**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest` | 1566 passed, 96.1% coverage |
| `vitest` | 450 passed |
| Playwright E2E + axe | 75 passed |
| `ruff` / `mypy` / `eslint` / `actionlint` | clean |
| `check_integrity.py` on current data | `status: ok`, 0 errors |
| Build with `site/public/` removed | builds clean |

This is a data-correctness bug, not a regression in the existing suites — no current test exercises a Workday tenant that nulls `locationsText`.

**Related, not the same issue:** #243 covers inconsistent *documentation* wording about US vs CA/IN scope. This issue is about the location *gate* being bypassed at runtime by postings that should have been excluded.

**Note on `/job/<Location>/` edge cases:** some segments are building-qualified rather than a clean city (e.g. `Warsaw-Sienna-39`, `Kronberg-Campus-Kronberg-1`, `Kuala-Lumpur-Vertical-Corp-Tower-B`). These still fail the gate correctly, so the fix is safe without a full place-name parser — but a follow-up cleanup for tidier display would be reasonable.

items.title: [ROADMAP] Help us expand job data — all suggestions welcome!
items.description:
## TL;DR

We want to dramatically expand the job data this project surfaces, and we need **your ideas**. Whether you have a small tweak, a wild idea, or a full proposal — drop it in the comments. **All suggestions are welcome and I will reply to every comment.**

---

## Why this roadmap?

New-Grad-Jobs is most useful when it captures the widest possible surface of legitimate new-grad opportunities. Today we scrape and curate from a known set of sources, but there's a long tail of companies, regions, and job types we're missing.

This issue is the central place to brainstorm **how we add more jobs** — sources, regions, scrapers, partnerships, automation, data quality, anything.

## What kind of suggestions are we looking for?

Pick whatever resonates — these are just prompts:

### Sources
- [ ] Specific ATS platforms we don't yet scrape (Workday tenants, Greenhouse boards, Lever, Ashby, SmartRecruiters, iCIMS, Taleo, Eightfold, Phenom, Jobvite, BrassRing, etc.)
- [ ] Specific companies whose new-grad pipelines we should track
- [ ] Regional job boards (EU, India, LATAM, MENA, APAC, Canada, UK, etc.)
- [ ] University career portals worth aggregating
- [ ] Government / public-sector hiring portals
- [ ] Startup-focused aggregators (YC, Wellfound, etc.)
- [ ] Diversity-focused or accessibility-focused boards

### Job categories
- [ ] Internship pipelines distinct from full-time
- [ ] PhD / research / quant-specific listings
- [ ] Hardware, semiconductor, robotics, aerospace
- [ ] Game industry
- [ ] Finance / trading / actuarial new-grad tracks
- [ ] Bio / pharma / healthcare new-grad roles
- [ ] Trades, ops, supply chain, manufacturing new-grad programs

### Data quality
- [ ] How should we detect & dedupe reposted listings?
- [ ] How should we classify \"new grad\" vs \"junior\" vs \"intern\" more accurately?
- [ ] Should we surface salary data when available? From which sources?
- [ ] Should we flag visa sponsorship / remote / hybrid more explicitly?
- [ ] How should we handle stale postings (last-seen vs first-seen)?
- [ ] What metadata is most useful to filter on?

### Infrastructure & automation
- [ ] Scraper frameworks or libraries worth adopting
- [ ] Anti-bot / rate-limit strategies that respect ToS
- [ ] Workflow scheduling improvements (cron, GitHub Actions, queues)
- [ ] LLM-assisted parsing for unstructured careers pages
- [ ] Storage / dedup / canonicalization approaches
- [ ] Notification channels (RSS, Discord, Slack, email digest)

### Community & contribution
- [ ] How can we make it easier for contributors to add a new company in one PR?
- [ ] Should we publish a contribution template specifically for \"add a company\"?
- [ ] Would a structured YAML/JSON registry of companies + ATS endpoints help?
- [ ] Mentorship for first-time contributors who want to add a scraper

## How to suggest

Just comment below. Any format works:

- **A single company:** \"Please add `<Company>` — their careers page is `<URL>`\"
- **A source idea:** \"There's an ATS called `<X>` used by these companies: …\"
- **A feature idea:** \"It would be great if listings showed `<field>`\"
- **A full proposal:** longer-form design ideas, link to a gist or doc
- **A pain point:** \"As a job seeker, I wish this repo did `<X>`\"

You don't need to know how to scrape, write Python, or anything technical. **Ideas count just as much as code.**

## Commitment

- I'll **reply to every comment on this thread.**
- Concrete, actionable suggestions will be moved into their own tracking issues and linked back here.
- Larger themes will become milestones on the roadmap.
- Credit will go to the suggester in the resulting PR / issue / changelog.

## Ground rules

- Be respectful — this is a community space.
- Don't post anything that violates a source's Terms of Service or robots.txt; we want sustainable, ethical aggregation.
- Don't post personal data, recruiter contacts, or anything that could harm a company or candidate.
- Prefer one idea per comment when possible — it makes follow-up easier.

---

**Thanks in advance — every suggestion helps a new grad find their first job.**

items.title: [Feature]: canonicalize job URLs before deduplication and job_id generation
items.description:
### Problem
Deduplication and `job_id` generation currently depend on raw URLs. Equivalent listings often differ only by tracking/query variants (for example `gh_jid`, UTM params, reordered query strings), which can produce duplicate jobs and unstable IDs for the same posting.

### Proposed Solution
Canonicalize URLs before passing them into dedup (`get_job_key`) and `compute_job_id` identity logic:
- normalize host/scheme casing
- remove known tracking params (for example UTM-style parameters)
- sort remaining query params deterministically
- trim safe trailing-slash noise

Use canonical URL for identity/dedup while preserving original apply URL as needed for display.

### Alternatives Considered
- Keep exact URL matching only (still allows duplicates from link variants).
- Use fuzzy title/company dedup only (higher false-positive risk than deterministic URL normalization).

### 🏗️ Which area does this affect?
🤖 Core scraper (scripts/update_jobs.py)

### Constraints Check
- [x] This does NOT require an external database (PostgreSQL, Redis, SQLite, etc.)
- [x] This does NOT require a frontend framework (React, Vue, Next.js, Tailwind)
- [x] This does NOT require an external orchestrator (Airflow, Celery, etc.)

items.title: [Advanced]: add iCIMS ingestion support to recover enterprise networking and infrastructure coverage
items.description:
### 🧠 Advanced Contributors
This issue is for contributors who are already very familiar with this codebase
and its architectural patterns.

You should feel comfortable:
- Understanding the full data flow: `config.yml` → fetch → filter → dedup → categorize → commit
- Reading and modifying `ThreadPoolExecutor` logic and thread-safety considerations
- Reasoning about API contract changes across ATS providers
- Writing rigorous, deterministic tests without live network calls

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **You must be assigned before starting** — comment `/assign` to claim this issue.
> PRs submitted without a prior assignment will be closed.

### 🐞 Problem Description
The roadmap already calls out ATS coverage expansion as the biggest remaining quality gap. Today, the scraper has strong coverage for Greenhouse, Lever, Google Careers, and partial Workday, but it still misses entire slices of enterprise hiring that sit behind other ATS platforms.

iCIMS is a high-leverage next source because it is common among larger employers, including companies that post entry-level infrastructure, networking, and security roles that never reach the board today.

Without a first-class iCIMS integration, the dataset will continue to under-represent one of the main role families the README says it tracks.

### 💡 Proposed / Expected Solution
Add a production-ready iCIMS fetch path that follows the same project constraints as the existing sources:

- config-driven company definitions
- deterministic tests with mocked responses
- compatibility with the current normalization, filtering, and dedup pipeline
- no external database or browser-based dependency

This should be implemented as a source integration, not as a one-off company patch.

### ✅ Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A reusable iCIMS fetch path exists in the scraper
- [ ] `config.yml` can declare iCIMS-backed companies without custom code per company
- [ ] New source behavior is covered by deterministic tests with mocked payloads
- [ ] Thread-safety is preserved
- [ ] All existing `pytest tests/` pass
- [ ] New tests added for every changed code path (deterministic — no live network calls)
- [ ] `pre-commit run --all-files` passes
- [ ] `jobs.json` schema remains backward compatible with `docs/app.js`
- [ ] PR is linked to this issue with `Fixes #<number>`
- [ ] PR title follows Conventional Commits format

### 🏗️ Which area does this touch?
🤖 Core scraper (scripts/update_jobs.py)

### 🔗 Additional Context
- Roadmap reference: `ROADMAP.md` lists iCIMS support under v1.1
- Existing ATS references: Greenhouse, Lever, Google Careers, Workday

items.title: [Intermediate]: Move hardcoded worker pool limits to config.yml
items.description:
---
## Thanks for contributing! 😊

This template creates an **Intermediate Issue** — for contributors who are already
comfortable navigating this codebase and contribution workflow.

The goal is a task that requires understanding existing patterns and making decisions,
but does not require architectural design from scratch.
---

### 🧩 Intermediate Contributors

This issue is intended for contributors who already have experience with this repository
and the contribution workflow.

You should feel comfortable:
- Navigating `scripts/update_jobs.py`, `config.yml`, and `tests/`
- Understanding how `filter_jobs()`, `deduplicate_jobs()`, and `categorize_job()` work
- Following existing patterns without step-by-step guidance
- Writing non-trivial pytest tests with mocking

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **You must be assigned before starting** — comment `/assign` to claim this issue.
> PRs submitted without a prior assignment will be closed.

If you are new to this repo, please start with a
[Good First Issue](https://github.com/ambicuity/New-Grad-Jobs/issues?q=is%3Aissue+state%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22+no%3Aassignee)
or a [Beginner Issue](https://github.com/ambicuity/New-Grad-Jobs/issues?q=is%3Aissue+state%3Aopen+label%3Abeginner+no%3Aassignee)
first.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> ### 🧭 What we consider an Intermediate Issue in this repo
>
> This issue generally:
> - Requires **knowledge of 2–3 existing functions** (e.g. `filter_jobs`, `normalize_date_string`, `get_job_key`)
> - Is **narrowly scoped** — touches one area without cascading structural changes
> - Is **medium risk** — does not change deduplication keys, date parsing logic from scratch, or pagination
> - May involve **refactors, edge case handling, or small feature additions**
> - Has **similar patterns elsewhere** in the scraper for reference
>
> **What this issue is NOT:**
> - A simple config addition (that belongs in Good First Issue)
> - A new scraping source integration (that belongs in Advanced)
> - A breaking change to the job schema


### 🐞 Problem Description

CodeRabbit flagged a major architectural debt item in PR #78: the scraper uses hardcoded concurrency limits (e.g., `max_workers = min(300, max(30, total // 3))`) in the `fetch_all_*_parallel` functions.

Hardcoding `max_workers=300` for Greenhouse risks IP bans if their rate limits change. The maintainer needs a way to throttle the scraper via configuration, not by pushing code.

### 💡 Expected Solution

These constants need to be moved to `config.yml` to allow for runtime tuning without code changes. Add a `worker_pools` block to `config.yml` with sub-keys for each API source.

- [ ] Add a `worker_pools` block to `config.yml`.

items.title: [Beginner]: Convert usa_states and usa_cities lists in is_valid_location() to frozenset for O(1) lookup
items.description:
## Summary

`is_valid_location()` in `scripts/update_jobs.py` stores USA state abbreviations and city names in **plain Python lists**. Every call performs a linear scan (`O(n)`) across 100+ entries. Converting to `frozenset` makes each lookup `O(1)` and is the idiomatic Python approach for membership testing.

## Location

`scripts/update_jobs.py`, function `is_valid_location()` (~line 1067)

```python
# Current — O(n) linear scan, called for every job
usa_states = [
    'alabama', 'al', 'alaska', 'ak', ...  # 102 entries, rebuilt per call
]
usa_cities = [
    'new york', 'los angeles', ...  # 42 entries, rebuilt per call
]
for state in usa_states:          # O(n) every time
    if state in location_lower:
        return True
```

## Expected Fix

Move the lists to **module-level constants** as `frozenset` (immutable, hashable):

```python
# At module level (top of file, after imports)
_USA_STATES: frozenset[str] = frozenset([
    'alabama', 'al', 'alaska', 'ak', ...
])
_USA_CITIES: frozenset[str] = frozenset([
    'new york', 'los angeles', ...
])
_CANADA_INDICATORS: frozenset[str] = frozenset([...])
_INDIA_INDICATORS: frozenset[str] = frozenset([...])

def is_valid_location(location: str) -> bool:
    ...
    # Now O(1) per check, and no list rebuild per call
    if any(state in location_lower for state in _USA_STATES):
        return True
```

## Why This Matters

`is_valid_location()` is called for **every job** in the pipeline (potentially thousands per run). Rebuilding these lists on the stack 10,000+ times per execution is unnecessary overhead. Module-level `frozenset` constants are constructed once at import time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `usa_states`, `usa_cities`, `canada_indicators`, `india_indicators` moved to module-level `frozenset` constants
- [ ] Named with leading underscore (e.g. `_USA_STATES`) to signal internal use
- [ ] `is_valid_location()` updated to use the new constants
- [ ] Existing behavior (returns `True`/`False`) is unchanged
- [ ] CI passes

## Skill Level

**Beginner** — Pure refactor: moving data from inside a function to module-level constants and changing `list` to `frozenset`. No logic changes required.

items.title: [Beginner]: Add module-level docstrings to CATEGORY_PATTERNS and company classification sets
items.description:
### Contributor Level

This is a beginner issue. No code logic changes are required. It is suitable for contributors who want to improve their understanding of the codebase before tackling more complex tasks.

Prerequisites:
- Able to read Python code and understand what a variable is used for
- Able to write a short English explanation

Estimated time to complete: 1 hour.

---

### Problem Description

The top-level global constants in `scripts/update_jobs.py` — specifically `FAANG_PLUS`, `UNICORNS`, `DEFENSE`, `FINANCE`, `HEALTHCARE`, `STARTUPS`, and `CATEGORY_PATTERNS` — have no inline comments or docstrings explaining what they represent, how they are consumed at runtime, or how a contributor should add a new entry to them.

A contributor who wants to add a new company has no guidance on which set to add it to, or how company classification interacts with the frontend filters. This increases the friction for community contributions of new company data.

Affected lines: approximately 93–254 in `scripts/update_jobs.py`.

---

### Proposed Solution

Add a short block comment above each constant explaining:

1. What the set represents
2. Which function consumes it at runtime
3. How to add a new entry, including the expected string format

Reference example:

```python
# FAANG_PLUS: Companies classified as the "FAANG+" company tier.
# Consumed by: get_company_tier() at line ~302.
# This classification surfaces in the frontend's "FAANG+" company-tier filter.
# To add a company: append its name exactly as it appears in job API responses.
# A company may appear in both FAANG_PLUS and a sector set (e.g., DEFENSE) simultaneously.
FAANG_PLUS = {
    ...
}
```

Apply the same pattern to: `UNICORNS`, `DEFENSE`, `FINANCE`, `HEALTHCARE`, `STARTUPS`, and `CATEGORY_PATTERNS`.

For `CATEGORY_PATTERNS`, also document how the `keywords` list is matched and what happens when no keyword matches.

---

### Background Research

Read the functions that consume these constants before writing comments:

- `get_company_tier()` — line ~302 (consumes `FAANG_PLUS`, `UNICORNS`, `DEFENSE`, `FINANCE`, `HEALTHCARE`, `STARTUPS`)
- `categorize_job()` — line ~278 (consumes `CATEGORY_PATTERNS`)

Understanding what these functions do with the data will help you write accurate descriptions.

---

### Acceptance Criteria

- A block comment appears above each of the seven constants listed above
- Each comment covers: purpose, consuming function, and how to add a new entry
- `python -m py_compile scripts/update_jobs.py` passes with no errors
- No logic is changed

---

### Done Checklist

Before opening your PR, confirm:

- [ ] All seven constants have a descriptive block comment above them
- [ ] `python -m py_compile scripts/update_jobs.py` passes locally
- [ ] Commit message follows Conventional Commits format: `docs(scraper): add comments to company classification constants`
- [ ] `README.md` has not been modified (it is auto-generated)

---

### Additional Context

- File: `scripts/update_jobs.py`, lines 93–254
- Related guide: [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/ambicuity/New-Grad-Jobs/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
